high_pH_nutrient_lockout_notes: Treat pH above about 7 as a nutrient availability risk, especially for micronutrients.
Elevated pH reduces solubility of iron, manganese, and zinc, which can limit uptake and quality.
low_pH_sensitivity_notes: In calibrated hydroponic lettuce systems, drifting outside the acceptable pH band increases deficiency risk.
Treat pH below the preferred band as a quality and nutrient-balance risk rather than an immediate lethal threshold.

growth_notes: Stage timing baseline: germination about 3 days, seedling phase about 10 days, then post-transplant growth to harvest about 30 to 40 days.
With proper management, yields of about 2 to 6 kg per square meter per crop cycle are reported.
Alternative production anchor: about 150 g marketable head at about 35 days after seeding under controlled CEA lighting conditions.
Hydroponic greenhouse baseline: germination about 3 days, seedling phase about 10 days, then post-transplant growth to harvest about 30 to 40 days.
stress_notes: Prolonged heat and high temperature fluctuations increase bolting risk, bitterness, and unmarketable crop output.
Tipburn is a calcium-related physiological disorder often driven by humid microclimates and low transpiration rather than low calcium supply alone.
Cooler low-light operation can still produce lettuce, but it slows time to harvest.
Treat calcium around 40 to 50 ppm as a starting management knob when tipburn risk is elevated by poor transpiration.

hydroponic_baseline.notes: Use as plant-optimized hydroponic lettuce baseline.
